title: Anjali Patil's Tamil Film 'Selvi' to World Premiere at Busan Film Festival
excerpt: The National Award-winning actress's debut production under Anahat Films will screen in Busan's Vision – Asia section in October, marking the banner's first Tamil feature.
body:
• National Film Award-winning actress Anjali Patil's Tamil film "Selvi" will have its world premiere at the 31st Busan International Film Festival in the Vision – Asia section, running October 6–15, 2026.
  • The film is the debut feature of Tamil writer-director Sailesh Rathnakumar, co-written with cinematographer Bargav Sridhar and edited by nine-time National Award winner A. Sreekar Prasad.
  • Produced under Patil's banner Anahat Films, "Selvi" is an India-Saudi Arabia co-production backed by the Red Sea Fund and Hong Kong Asia Film Financing.
  • "Selvi" follows a home-care nurse navigating caregiving, migration, and survival — inspired by real nurses who cared for Sridhar's critically ill mother.

National Film Award-winning actress Anjali Patil's Tamil-language film "Selvi" has been selected for its world premiere at the 31st Busan International Film Festival, organisers confirmed this week. The film will screen in the Vision – Asia section, Busan's platform for new Asian directors and one of the most closely watched discovery slots in world cinema.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=HBbuP9x1cls

The festival runs from October 6 to 15, 2026, in South Korea's second-largest city.

A Story Born From Real Lives

"Selvi" marks the feature debut of Tamil writer-director Sailesh Rathnakumar. Co-written with cinematographer Bargav Sridhar, the film was inspired by the home-care nurses who attended Sridhar's mother through months of critical illness — migrant women from smaller towns in Tamil Nadu, living in modest hostels, working daily in homes nothing like their own.

The film follows its titular character, a home-care nurse navigating the weight of caregiving, duty, and survival while managing her own family's needs and personal dreams. It explores care, migration, friendship, guilt, and exhaustion through the lens of a largely invisible workforce.

"Selvi is about a woman moving through an ordinary day. I wanted the film to move with her, to stay close to her life without explaining it or asking it to mean more than it already does."

— Sailesh Rathnakumar, Director

The cast includes Archana Padmini, Anjali Patil in the titular role, and Vinoth Kishan. The film was edited by A. Sreekar Prasad, a nine-time National Film Award winner, with sound design by Anand Krishnamurthy and music by Suren Vikhash.

Anahat Films' Growing International Footprint

Patil produced "Selvi" under her banner Anahat Films, which she founded in 2021. The production house has built a track record at top-tier international festivals: its previous projects include "The Moogai," which premiered at Sundance in 2023, and "Baksho Bondi," which was showcased at the Berlinale in 2025. "Selvi" is Anahat Films' first full-length Tamil feature.

The film is an India-Saudi Arabia co-production, backed by the Red Sea Fund — an initiative of the Red Sea International Film Festival — and supported by Hong Kong Asia Film Financing after being selected at the 24th HAF.

"Selvi became my way of reclaiming creative independence for stories that need patience to be told. It's a personal, intimate observation of the ordinary people in healthcare who spend their lives caring for others, even as their own lives quietly wither."

— Anjali Patil, Lead Actress and Producer

Indian Cinema's Growing Presence at Global Festivals

Patil, known for her roles in critically acclaimed films such as "Newton" (2017) and Rajinikanth-starrer "Kaala" (2018), has steadily positioned herself as both an actor and producer championing independent Indian cinema on global stages. Her dual role in "Selvi" — as lead performer and producer — reflects a broader trend of Indian actors taking creative and financial ownership of projects aimed at international audiences.

The Busan International Film Festival, Asia's largest, has become an increasingly important launchpad for Indian independent cinema. The selection of "Selvi" adds to a growing list of Indian films finding audience and critical attention at premier international festivals, signaling the global appetite for stories from the subcontinent that go beyond mainstream Bollywood fare.

What's Next

Following its Busan premiere in October, "Selvi" is expected to make the rounds at additional international festivals before a theatrical release. Patil has said she plans to bring the film "back home, to the people to whom it truly belongs," according to IANS.
